headline: Ben Johnson's bet on shared records
mechanism: Scaffold will use seed proceeds to expand AI that structures construction documents and coordinates purchase orders and schedules across existing builder, contractor and supplier systems. The picture keeps each plan sheet in place, carries markup across dashed bridges rather than replacing any sheet, and ends the schedule bar with no completion marker because the dossier sets no completion deadline.
silhouette: four offset plan sheets in steep perspective joined by dashed bridges and an open schedule bar

visual_anchors.claim: HousingWire reports that AI structures data from scanned documents and that schedule changes can affect billing and job costs.
visual_anchors.drawn_as: floor plan sheet at the back, with the copper thread leaving it to reach the purchase order

visual_anchors.claim: The existing product connects existing systems rather than requiring their replacement. Manual entry and another separate application are source-described alternatives.
visual_anchors.drawn_as: one continuous copper thread through all three sheets, with no sheet replaced

visual_anchors.claim: Proceeds are intended to expand engineering and coverage of builder, contractor and supplier systems. No hiring quota or completion deadline is given.
